chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: A man from your mawla (clients/freemen) died, leaving behind young children, and he left some property, and he had a debt, but the creditors did not know about it. If the debt is paid to the creditors, his children will be left with nothing. He said: 'Spend it on his children.'
The book of Al-Wasa'ila (or Al-Wasiyya) ended, and praise be to God with true praise.
ai.seo_question: How should an estate be distributed if the deceased has young children and an unknown debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a pragmatic solution for estates with minor heirs and undisclosed debts, ruling to 'spend it on the children' rather than exhausting assets on creditors who may not claim their due. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing the immediate welfare of dependents (*nafaqa*) over the rights of creditors when the latter are unknown or unclaimed. The ruling underscores the balance between fulfilling financial obligations and preserving the lineage's sustenance, a key consideration in *Fiqh al-Mirath*.
